newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament backs sending troops to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament backs sending troops to Albania.

text.p: Turkey's parliament voted on Thursday in favour of a government plan to send troops to Albania to participate in a multinational peacekeeping force aimed at protecting humanitarian relief operations there.
Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan announced last week that Turkey would send 500 troops to Albania.

"Turkey is following a movement whose priority is to provide peace and stability in Albania. Albania is an important country with whom Turkey will develop its relations," State Minister Serif Ercan said, announcing the parliament's decision.

The 6,000-strong Italian-led multinational force, involving troops from Italy, France, Spain, Turkey, Greece and Romania, is expected to start arriving in Albania on Monday to protect the delivery of emergency food and medical supplies.

Albania, Europe's poorest country, plunged into near chaos when get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes collapsed and armed rebels took control of the south during an unchecked spasm of looting and banditry.
More than 200 people have been killed and about 700 injured in the violence. Army arsenals were looted after soldiers and police abandoned their posts and citizens seized thousands of weapons.
